items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: he told me, Jack Teagarden, Barney Begard, and Sidney Catlett. And, the only one I didn't know was Arwell Shaw

ctx.x: And it was a black theater and I used to come out of, out of class and go across the street to the theater all the time, because I knew a lot of the musicians that were, that were playing in the, in the show. And it was during the time when I had first started doing jazz concerts. So it was 1936 and I went backstage, because his band was playing there. And I knew Louis Russell and Red Allen and people that were playing there, Al Nicholas. So, I had, I had met Louis before, I don't actually remember when, but…
Okay, we're on the second reel. Al Rose, same date. August 13th, 1989. Okay, we left off with Eus... Eus Panassia.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: I proposed that the newly organized band of Jack Teagarden would be, uh, attractive to, to bring in.

ctx.x: But even among these people, there was a consciousness of the personalities and the people that had recorded the early jazz. Some of those people, of course, were playing in swing bands. And the fact that I had this collection became very well known in school, and people used to come to my room all the time to listen to records. And to discuss with me the music that they were playing, and they were much interested in this. Well, in 1935, the American Newspaper Guild was about to, was planning an annual affair.…
Now, had you done any of this kind of thing before?
